title: Prefetch policy overshoot — end-to-end latency and early-EOS investigation
content:
Summary:

During a staged rollout of an updated KV-prefetch policy (prefetch_window_tokens: 1024, adaptive_prefetch: enabled), on Nov 2nd we observed an unexpected regression in tail latency (p95+p99) and an increase in short-generation early-EOS occurrences for select chat routes. The change was intended to improve throughput for long-context workloads by prefetching additional key/value shards, but the policy overshot in production when the canary flag was accidentally flipped to global by a CI configuration bug.

Impact:
- Time window: 2025-11-02 15:14 UTC — 2025-11-02 16:46 UTC (approx).
- Affected surface: hosted text-generation and chat routes pinned to model family rwd-13b-v2 in us-west-2.
- Symptom A: p95 token-latency increased from ~18ms to ~48ms, p99 from ~45ms to ~120ms.
- Symptom B: Early-EOS events (client-visible premature end-of-sequence) rose from 0.04% to 1.2% of completions on affected routes.
- User-visible impact: intermittent truncation of assistant responses and elevated latencies for a subset of sessions (approx 2k requests/min at peak). No data exfiltration or model-corruption observed.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-02 14:55 UTC — rollout CI job merged and annotated as staged (PR merged: runtime#9878).
- 2025-11-02 15:12 UTC — canary hosts in us-west-2 started receiving new prefetch config. Initial telemetry looked fine.
- 2025-11-02 15:14 UTC — configuration flag propagation mis-routed due to a templating bug in infra-deploy, marking the feature as enabled for the entire fleet instead of canary.
- 2025-11-02 15:28 UTC — first SLO alert: route token-latency p95 breach (datadog alert token-latency-p95).
- 2025-11-02 15:33 UTC — on-call SRE (Ravi) paged; investigation begins.
- 2025-11-02 15:40 UTC — spikes in worker mem pressure and KV cache fill rate noticed on affected nodes.
- 2025-11-02 15:54 UTC — evidence of increased microbatch queuing and slower kernel selection times.
- 2025-11-02 16:02 UTC — early-EOS incidents correlated with prefetch window crossing a boundary in tokenizer state for certain prefix lengths.
- 2025-11-02 16:16 UTC — temporary mitigation: feature-flag rollback triggered (infra-deploy revert), fleet gradually returned to baseline.

Root cause analysis:
1) Config-gating bug: The CI templating step that generates canary rollout manifests had a variable interpolation error. A boolean intended to scope the change to canary labels (env.canary_only = true) evaluated to false during templating, producing manifests that omitted the canary selector. As a result, all nodes received prefetch policy changes simultaneously.

2) Policy mismatch with model runtime heuristics: The new policy set prefetch_window_tokens=1024 (designed for long-context inference) while the runtime’s internal prefix-length estimator assumes canonical_max_prefetch=128 for rwd-13b-v2. This mismatch caused aggressive shard prefetch across many requests with short prefixes, increasing memory pressure and triggering subtler scheduling side-effects (microbatch reorderings).

3) Boundary interaction causing early-EOS: For some prefix/tokenization edge cases (routes with a trailing soft-prompt marker and certain unicode punctuation), the prefetch-induced reordering changed the timing of KV cache availability and led to the runtime taking a fast-path that used an outdated attention-mask length. That fast-path emitted an EOS token earlier than the slower, correct code path would have. This behavior only surfaced under high microbatching pressure and with the larger prefetch window.

Why the canary didn’t catch it:
- Canary sampling was limited to 2 hosts per AZ; the templating bug caused the canary selector to be dropped from the manifest, so monitoring dashboards were showing canary metrics as expected but the actual rollout happened fleet-wide.
- Synthetic canary tests focused on throughput and token-accuracy on long-context prompts, not on combined short-prefix + punctuation edgecases.

Mitigation and recovery:
- 2025-11-02 16:20 UTC — emergency rollback executed (infra-deploy revert to commit prior to PR #9878).
- 2025-11-02 16:40 UTC — rollout fully reverted; by 16:46 UTC p95/p99 latencies returned to baseline and early-EOS rate fell back to normal.
- Short-term: throttled rate of concurrent batch size (microbatch_max_concurrency) reduced from 64 to 32 for rwd-13b-v2 until further tunings completed.

Observations from post-incident traces and logs:
- Kernel selection latencies increased by ~2.5x during the incident window due to extra shard activation work.
- KV cache fill-rate spiked and eviction churn increased on the affected nodes.
- GC-like memory reclamation cycles (runtime-level) increased during the spike; observed more transient memory pressure logs.
- Affected requests skewed to short prefix lengths (<64 tokens) even though prefetch window was large — confirming policy overshoot.

Detection and monitoring improvements recommended:
- Add a rollout manifest lint step in CI that asserts "canary_selector" field presence and validates boolean interpolation for canary_only. (owner: platform-eng, owner_alias: Maya Chen, due: 2025-11-12)
- New Datadog synthetic check: run a short-prefix + unicode-punct test case at pre-rollout time and measure early-EOS delta; fail the rollout if early-EOS delta > 0.2%.
- Add an alert for mismatch between prefetch_window_tokens and runtime-reported canonical_prefetch_hint per model family (alert when ratio > 4x).
- Add an internal metric 'prefetch_effective_shard_load' that measures extra shard activation cycles per request and alert once it crosses threshold for >5m.

Runbook changes / Playbook additions:
- Playbook: "prefetch-policy-regression.md" (new) — steps to triage prefetch-induced latency regressions, with exact queries and commands. Key runbook snippets below. (owner: eng-sre, Samir Patel, due: 2025-11-09)

  Quick triage commands (examples):
  - Datadog: token-latency.p95{env:prod,model:rwd-13b-v2}.rollup(avg,60)
  - Query KV stats (prod-monitoring cluster): SELECT time, shard_activations, evictions_per_min FROM kv_metrics WHERE model='rwd-13b-v2' AND region='us-west-2' AND time BETWEEN X AND Y
  - Runtime debug endpoint: /debug/prefetch_state?node=<node-id> (requires internal cert).

  Immediate mitigations:
  - If prefetch_policy unexpectedly flips: set env var PREFETCH_OVERRIDE=0 and trigger infra-deploy revert.
  - To reduce impact while investigating: reduce microbatch_max_concurrency and prefetch_window_tokens to safe defaults (128).

Postmortem action items (with owners):
- CI templating validation: add unit tests and a manifest linter ensuring canary selectors are present (owner: platform-eng — Maya Chen — due 2025-11-12).
- Runtime-preflight tests: add synthetic suite covering short-prefix + punctuation triggers for all model families before rollout (owner: developer-experience — Elena Ruiz — due 2025-11-19).
- Prefetch policy safety caps: enforce server-side hard cap prefetch_window_tokens <= 256 unless model opt-in via model metadata (owner: serving-runtime — Owen Brooks — due 2025-11-16).
- Add telemetry label to deployments showing which manifest commit caused config change, surfaced in dashboards (owner: release-engineering — Samir Patel — due 2025-11-20).
- Post-incident knowledge share: run a 30-min "what happened" session for SRE+runtime teams (owner: Ravi Desai — scheduled 2025-11-07).

Lessons learned:
- Cross-layer assumptions matter: infra manifest shape, CI templating, model-specific runtime heuristics all interacted. A small omission in templating cascaded to a cross-stack production outage.
- Canary is only as good as its selection plumbing and tests. Canary sampling must be validated end-to-end (selection, routing, and synthetic behavioral checks).
- Prefetch heuristics improve throughput for long sequences but add a combinatorial risk surface when combined with microbatch scheduling and tokenizer edgecases.

Appendix: data snapshots (aggregated) during peak of incident:
- Token-latency p50: 12ms -> 14ms (small change)
- Token-latency p95: 18ms -> 48ms (regression)
- Token-latency p99: 45ms -> 120ms (regression)
- Early-EOS rate: 0.04% -> 1.2% (absolute increase ~1.16pp)
- KV shard activations per request: 1.2 -> 3.8 (avg)

Related tickets and PRs:
- JIRA-SRE-4321 (incident triage)
- runtime PR #9878 (prefetch policy change)
- infra-deploy PR #9902 (revert commit)

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Investigate whether a per-route model metadata flag (e.g., route_metadata.prefetch_sensitive=true) is feasible to opt certain flows out of aggressive prefetching.
- Confirm whether other model families have similar fast-paths vulnerable to ordering differences; prioritize a quick audit of rwd-7b and rwd-20b codepaths.

End of document.
